name: David Brooks
bio: a Representative from New York; born in Philadelphia, Pa., in 1756; attended the public schools; served in the Revolutionary War, entered the Continental Army as a lieutenant in the Pennsylvania Battalion of the Flying Camp in 1776; was captured at Fort Washington, November 16, 1776, and exchanged in January 1780; appointed assistant clothier general for the Continental Army; studied law; was admitted to the bar and practiced; after the war settled in New York County, N.Y.; member of the New York assembly, 1787 and 1788; moved to Dutchess County, N.Y.; member of the New York state assembly, 1794-1796 and 1810; judge of Dutchess County,N.Y., 1795-1807; elected as a Federalist to the Fifth Congress (March 4, 1797-March 3, 1799); unsuccessful candidate for reelection to the Sixth Congress in 1798; unsuccessful candidate for election to the Seventh Congress in 1800; appointed commissioner to negotiate a treaty with the Seneca Indians; clerk of Dutchess County, N.Y., June 5, 1807, to January 25, 1809 and from February 9, 1810, to February 14, 1811, and again from February 23, 1813, to February 13, 1815; appointed an officer in the United States Customs Service; an original member of the Society of the Cincinnati; died on August 30, 1838, in Poughkeepsie, Dutchess County, N.Y.; interment probably in the Old Rural Cemetery.
